title: Daily Outdoor Distance Viewing
description: Spend time outdoors looking at distant objects to support healthy eye development, reduce myopia risk, and provide natural light exposure for circadian health.

actions.details: Spend time outdoors looking at objects at least 20 feet away. Walk, sit in a park, or engage in outdoor activities while consciously viewing distant landscapes, trees, or horizon.
Engage in outdoor sports, hiking, or activities that naturally require distance viewing like tennis, golf, or nature walks.

benefits: Reduces risk of myopia development and progression
Provides natural bright light exposure (2000+ lux)
Improves overall eye health and visual development
Enhances depth perception and spatial awareness
Reduces indoor air pollution exposure for eyes
science: Outdoor light exposure of 1000-10000+ lux stimulates dopamine release in the retina, which inhibits axial eye growth and myopia development. Time spent outdoors is strongly protective against myopia regardless of near work activity levels.
contraindications: Use UV protection in very bright conditions
